items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:20:1
items.html: The light of the Einayim of AK is extended through there, it will mingle with them and take their light: As above in the adjacent item, that the forces that are in the upper one are necessarily obligated in the lower one. And this is what he says: “It is necessary that when the light of the Einayim is extended, etc., it will take their light.” That is to say, the light of the Einayim that the Nekudim receive necessarily passes through the AHP, and therefore it is necessary that the light of the Einayim take their light, for it will act according to the order of their vessels, and will divide upon those three discernments that are in the AHP of the Dikna [beard], and will transfer them to the discernment of the vessels of Nekudim. And you must likewise remember that every upper one is the discernment of an Emanator to the lower one and the discernment of the cause to the lower one; and accordingly the AHP of the Dikna are found to be the discernment of an Emanator to the ten Sefirot of Nekudim. Understand this.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:20:2
items.html:
The first three among them take light from what is extended from the look of the eye at AHP, from their place down to the place of their conjunction at the Shibolet of the beard. You already know that three discernments are discerned in every Partzuf that is drawn from the light of the Einayim: two discernments, Rosh [head] and Guf [body], are discerned in the ten Sefirot of the Rosh itself, which are Galgalta and Einayim for the Rosh and AHP for the Guf; and the third discernment is the actual Guf, which is called the seven lower Sefirot. This is after the manner explained in the adjacent item concerning the hairs of the Dikna [beard], study it there. And in this very same way the Nekudim too are divided.
And the first discernment of Nekudim, which is the discernment of the Galgalta and Einayim in them, that is, the Rosh of the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, is the one called Israel Saba and Tevuna, and its place is above the Tabur, up to the Chazeh. And of it the ARI says above, page 407, item 17: “All the light that is extended down to the Tabur, even though it is of the discernment of the Einayim, is all swallowed up and included in the Akudim, and therefore it is not recognisable,” study it there. And you will see that the ARI stresses that even though it is of the discernment of the Einayim, it is nevertheless reckoned as Akudim and not as Nekudim. And the reason for this is that the coarseness in the screen does not act at all at the time when it serves from below upward; and since this YESHSUT is the discernment of the true Rosh of Nekudim, that is, the Galgalta and Einayim, while the screen of the coarseness that is associated of phase two and phase four stands below, in the Nikvey Einayim of YESHSUT, which is the place of the point of the Tabur, therefore no recognition whatsoever of the association with phase four, which is drawn from the light of the Einayim, acts in it. And therefore it is discerned as the discernment of Akudim, like SAG, in which nothing is recognisable but phase two, and there is in it no recognition at all of the coarseness of Nekudim. And this is what he says, “that it is swallowed up and included in the Akudim, and therefore it is not recognisable.” And behold, the first discernment of the Partzuf of Nekudim has been explained: that it is called Israel Saba and Tevuna, and it is included in the Akudim.
And the second discernment of the Partzuf of Nekudim is the discernment of the AHP that go outside the Rosh and are discerned as its Guf, and this is by their being receivers of and clothing for the light that is drawn from the Nikvey Einayim, as above in the second discernment of the Dikna, which is called the Shibolet of the beard, which is the place of gathering for the lights of the AHP in the place of their emergence, study it there well. And remember and understand these outer AHP, that in their source they are truly Bina and ZA and Malchut of the Rosh, together with the Keter and Hochma that are in the first Rosh called YESHSUT; only from the aspect of their receiving the light of the Einayim did they go out from the law of a Rosh and become a Guf, and therefore they are called the second Rosh in relation to YESHSUT, which is called the first Rosh. And this second Rosh is the Rosh of Nekudim, which is called the GAR [first three] of Nekudim; but the first Rosh, which is YESHSUT, is reckoned as Akudim and not as Nekudim, as above in the words of the ARI, study it there.
And the third discernment of Nekudim is the discernment of the true Guf of Nekudim, meaning that they are beneath the Peh [mouth] of the Rosh, like the earlier Gufim in the Partzufim of AK. And they are called the seven lower Sefirot of Nekudim, similar to the corrections of the Dikna that are found below the Shibolet of the beard, which are extended down to the Chazeh and down to the Tabur; for the secret of the upper surface of the Dikna is extended to the Chazeh, and the secret of the lower surface of the Dikna is extended to the Tabur, by reason of their being the discernment of the seven lower Sefirot of the Dikna, which are ZA, that includes the six Sefirot HGT NHY, with Malchut as the seventh. And the upper surface of the Dikna is the six Sefirot called ZA, which is drawn from the Hotem of the Rosh, as is known from the preceding parts; and therefore it concludes at the Chazeh, for from the Chazeh to the Shibolet of the beard is the place of ZA, as is known. And the lower surface of the Dikna is the Malchut, whose vessel is from the Chazeh to the Tabur, and therefore it concludes at the Tabur. And in this same way are the seven lower Sefirot of Nekudim, which are ZA, that includes six Sefirot, with Malchut as the seventh.
And this is what he says: “The first three among them take light from what is extended from the look of the eye at AHP, from their place down to the place of their conjunction at the Shibolet of the beard.” As has been explained, the GAR of Nekudim are the discernment of the AHP that go outside the Rosh, which become a vessel of reception for the light that descends from above downward from the Nikvey Einayim of the first Rosh, similar to the Shibolet of the beard, which receives from the discernment of the Nikvey Einayim of the first Rosh of the Dikna — these being the AHP in their own place, that is, the three upper corrections of the Dikna that hang upon the very Rosh, above the Peh: the two borders of the Dikna on the right and on the left, below the Ozen; and the hairs of the upper lip that are above the Peh, on the right and on the left; and the Orcha [path] that is free of hairs, in the middle of the upper lip. And these three are called the AHP in their own place, whose meaning is that they are above the Peh, since the Malchut in them is still of the discernment of from below upward, in the secret of the upper jaw, and they are the discernment of the Galgalta and Einayim, whose screen is in the Einayim, which is the discernment of the upper lip. But the Shibolet of the beard, which is joined to the lower lip, is already the discernment of a Guf, though of the discernment of the AHP that went outside the Rosh. And it is known that the whole quantity of light that is in the Rosh of the Partzuf descends and is bestowed upon the Guf, as above in the parts. And it turns out that all the lights of the three upper corrections of the Dikna, which are the discernment of the AHP in their own place, descend and are bestowed and joined at the Shibolet of the beard. And this is what he says, that in the Shibolet of the beard there are joined all the continuation of the lights of the AHP in their own place, down to the Shibolet. And from it come the GAR of Nekudim, as has been explained. And remember these words for the whole continuation of the words of the ARI.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:20:3
items.html: And they receive them only at the Shibolet of the beard, for from there they begin. It has already been explained at length that the GAR of Nekudim are not the discernment of the true Rosh of the Partzuf of Nekudim, but they are the discernment of the second Rosh, which is the discernment of the AHP that go outside the first Rosh, and they are the discernment of the Shibolet of the beard. And this is what he says: “For from there they begin, and not from what is above the Shibolet of the beard.” For above the Shibolet of the beard is the discernment of the first Rosh, and from there the first Rosh of Nekudim, which is YESHSUT, receives — but not the GAR of Nekudim, who have no hold there, since in relation to it they are the discernment of a Guf, as has been explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:20:4
items.html: The seven lower Nekudot take only from what is extended from the look at the lights of the Hotem and the Peh, from the Shibolet of the beard downward. For it has been explained that the seven Nekudot are the discernment of the true Guf of the Partzuf of Nekudim, that is, the third discernment mentioned above, study it there. And therefore they receive from below the Shibolet of the beard, which is from the two surfaces of the Dikna [beard] down to the Chazeh and down to the Tabur, for they are the discernment of the seven lower Sefirot, as above.
